projects.title: Projects
projects.intro: Here's the work I'm proudest of.

tesi.desc: Recovering fault friction parameters from simulated earthquakes with convolutional neural networks
tesi.problem: A fault's friction properties (b, Dc and σn) can't be measured directly in the field, yet they set the critical nucleation length h*, the scale beyond which a seismic rupture becomes self-sustaining. The thesis tests whether a neural network can recover these parameters from spatio-temporal slip-rate maps generated with the quasi-dynamic simulator QDYN.
tesi.mine: Individual project: I generated the dataset with QDYN, designed and trained the CNNs and wrote the single-event parameter estimation.
tesi.result: Relative error of about 6% on Dc and 20% on b; σn, treated as binary classification, reaches 75% accuracy. The resulting estimate of h* has a mean error of about 0.03 cm.

retroshop.desc: A marketplace for retro games and consoles, with user listings and real-time chat
retroshop.problem: Project for the Web Technologies and Systems course: a complete website, from database to interface, for buying and selling retrogaming items.
retroshop.mine: Authentication, user profile, search and filters, checkout flow.
retroshop.result: React and Bootstrap interface, FastAPI backend, PostgreSQL database managed with SQLAlchemy, and user-to-user chat over WebSocket.

from-music-to-image.desc: Generating new Pokémon from a piece of music or a text description
from-music-to-image.problem: Second-year Machine Learning course project, built with Giacomo Tronca. The idea is to turn unconventional inputs, such as an audio file or a text, into sprites of never-seen creatures, using a dataset of 500+ Pokémon with sprites, cries and descriptions.
from-music-to-image.mine: I handled the music side: from the audio features of the tracks to sprite generation. The text side was handled by Giacomo Tronca.
from-music-to-image.result: We compared RealNVP, VAE, VAE-GAN and LoRA fine-tuning of Stable Diffusion: for music input the VAE gave the best results, while for text the final choice was a model conditioned on description embeddings.

tsunami-assessment.desc: Telling in real time whether an earthquake can trigger a tsunami
tsunami-assessment.problem: Project for the Earthquake Physics for Machine Learning course. Traditional warning systems have to wait for a full estimate of the earthquake before raising the alarm. The project uses Japan Meteorological Agency data (86,000+ events) to assess tsunami risk right after the shock.
tsunami-assessment.mine: Individual project: JMA data preparation, a multi-input LSTM on simulated data and a class-weighted Random Forest on historical data.
tsunami-assessment.result: On real test data the model detects 61.5% of tsunamis with 99.9% overall accuracy. Recall is the main metric, because a missed warning costs far more than a false alarm.

gnn-graph-coloring.desc: Graph coloring with Graph Neural Networks, starting from the Potts model
gnn-graph-coloring.problem: Project for the Physics Applications to Machine Learning course, with Sofia De Angelis, Matteo Pinato and Aurora Giaccherini. Graph coloring is NP-hard: we turned it into a differentiable optimization, with a loss that relaxes the antiferromagnetic Potts Hamiltonian plus an entropy term.
gnn-graph-coloring.mine: A fully shared team effort: we built the model, loss, experiments and analysis of the results together.
gnn-graph-coloring.result: Two architectures (GraphSAGE and GCN) compared on the DIMACS instances g9 and g15: chromatic number estimated by sweeping k from 2 to 15, benchmarked against the classic DSATUR heuristic.
